## Hypothesis

The weekly-1 DTE (1-2 DTE) setting of the WEEKLY_DTE_NOT_0DTE candidate captures a persistent edge of $59-66 per trade with statistical significance p<=0.045 over the last 6 months of SPY data, as previously reported. This OOS validation will confirm whether the edge holds out-of-sample and is not an artifact of in-sample overfit.

## Mechanism

Use the same directional signal as the base WEEKLY_DTE_NOT_0DTE candidate: buy the same directional signal at longer DTE (1-2 day weekly) instead of 0DTE; same strike (ITM-2) + same exit (-8%/+30%). The only change is to restrict the DTE filter to exactly 1-2 days to expiration (weekly-1 series). Entry triggers and exit logic remain identical; the DTE variable is isolated.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline (per OP-20 disclosure #1). The weekly-1 DTE setting will likely have different premium levels; we assume similar ITM-2 strike pricing.
2. **Sample bias:** The last 6 months of SPY data (approx 120 trading days) will be used for OOS test. Selection method: fixed time window (most recent 6 months) to avoid lookahead bias. Overfit risk: medium, as we are validating a previously reported edge on a holdout period.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (this candidate proposes to run the OOS test; result pending).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (validation will use realistic OPRA simulator; real-fills check pending).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: potential large loss if the signal fails during a volatile regime; max drawdown could exceed 50% of allocated capital; blow-up scenario: consecutive losing days eroding the edge due to regime shift or mis-specified DTE filter.
6. **Concentration:** If validated, we will disclose the top-5 days contribution to P&L; currently unknown.
